claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under the age of 16, or children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 18.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 18, I need to understand his current situation to assess your eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as school, college, university, or an apprenticeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and he's working full-time now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I need to ask one more important question about Alex's work:

**How many hours per week is Alex working, and is he getting any benefits in his own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's working full-time - about 24 hours or more each week. And no, he's not getting any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Based on what you've told me, I can now assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

According to the Child Benefit rules, you would **not be eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex because:

- Alex is 18 years old and no longer in approved education or training
- He is working 24 hours or more per week
- The rules state that Child Benefit stops when a child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training

Since Alex doesn't meet the eligibility criteria, you cannot claim Child Benefit for him.

Is there anything else you'd like me to clarify about the Child Benefit rules, or do you have any other children you'd like me to assess?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, that's all I needed to know. Thank you for explaining that to me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're welcome! I'm glad I could help explain the situation clearly. If you have any other questions about Child Benefit in the future, feel free to reach out.

Now let me record the outcome of this assessment:

reasonings: Alex is 18 years old and working full-time (24 hours or more per week). According to Child Benefit rules, eligibility for children aged 16 or over continues only if they remain in approved education or training. Since Alex has finished school and is no longer in education or training, and he is working 24 hours or more per week, he does not qualify for Child Benefit.
arguments.overall_reasoning: The claimant has one child, Alex, who is 18 years old and working full-time. Alex does not qualify for Child Benefit because he is neither in approved education or training nor meets any other qualifying criteria for children aged 16-19. Therefore, the claimant is not eligible for Child Benefit.
